item.title: 2026 archaka state
item.description:
Former state

Years ago each sivan temple in Thanjavur Jilla had a dedicated Kurukkal. They lived in Agraharam,took care of the presiding deity, did nithyapadi poojai, 4 kala poojai,6 kaala poojai,as the case may be. Each Vaishnava temple had a dedicated Archagar. They followed the agamam,performed thirumanajanam on Thirunakshathram etc., Mahasamprokshanam,Samvathsaram were done as per the tradition. Over the years,due to many reasons, the situation has changed.

Current state

Today in and around Kumbakonam,Thanjavur side you have one Kurukkal servicing 6,7 or even 8 temples. The impact is two ways.

item.title: Chidambaram sc judgement
item.description:
Source: TW

Ten year ago on this day - 06th Janauary 2014 - One of the finest judgments concerning Hindu Communities’ fundamental rights to administer and maintain their temples was delivered by Hon’ble Justice B.S. Chauhan and Hon’ble Justice S.A. Bobde in Hon’ble Supreme Court of India. The judgment while established or rather re-established the fundamental religious and administrative rights of the ancient community of Podhu Dikshitars of Chidambaram Sri Nataraja Temple - also enunciated when, if at all, a Hindu Temple’s administration can be taken over and for how long.

item.title: HRCE curbing
item.description:
Trustees

The Madras High Court’s recent ruling in a PIL related to the Sri Parthasarathy Swamy Temple, Thiruvallikeni filed by our President Shri @trramesh marks a welcome legal development.

The case raises an important question of temple governance: can an Executive Officer/Fit Person, who is a Government servant, continue to run an ancient temple in the absence of a duly appointed Board of Trustees?

This is not a mere technicality. Trustees play a crucial role in protecting temple property, funds, rituals, customs, festivals, and devotee rights. When temples are run indefinitely through temporary administrative arrangements, accountability and transparency suffer.

item.title: TN Temple control
item.description:
Source: Sreedharan K S (@SreedharanKs)

In this interview @RangarajPandeyR asked @jsaideepak why Justice Party wanted Govt Control of Temples, as they were the rich people administering temples. Here is some history.

In early 19th century EIC had nominal control over temples, till it relinquished in 1863 by Act XX. The temples became one of the power centres. Where there was no Zamindar, Pandarasandhi, rich and powerful people got themselves associated with temples. The financial power of Temples were so great that invariably the politicians got involved. To get an idea of the Temple wealth, some of the big temples and adheenams had lot of property and money. Because of the lacunae in the Act XX, the temple and its properties were not managed well and it was very difficult to take a legal recourse. (Not all temples were under Jameens. Where there was no pre-existing setup, the management was arbitrarily given. The troubles arose because those who thought they had the rights, fought amongst themselves. There was misuse and murders in Adheenams in some cases.)
